author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
review: 'The Great Gatsby' by F. Scott Fitzgerald is a timeless masterpiece that delves into the decadence and disillusionment of the Jazz Age. Set in the Roaring Twenties, the novel unveils the enigmatic Jay Gatsby's extravagant parties.

author: Harper Lee
review: 'To Kill a Mockingbird' is a gripping, heart-wrenching, and wholly remarkable tale of coming-of-age in a South poisoned by virulent prejudice.

author: George Orwell
review: '1984' is a dystopian novel by English author George Orwell. It was published on 8 June 1949 by Secker & Warburg as Orwell's ninth and final book completed in his lifetime.

author: J.D. Salinger
review: 'The Catcher in the Rye' is J.D. Salinger's 1951 novel of partial story about Holden Caulfield and teenage angst.

author: Jane Austen
review: 'Pride and Prejudice' is an 1813 romantic novel of manners written by Jane Austen. The novel follows the character development of Elizabeth Bennet.

author: J.R.R. Tolkien
review: 'The Hobbit' is a children's fantasy novel by English author J. R. R. Tolkien. It was published on 21 September 1937 to wide critical acclaim.

bookName: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone
author: J.K. Rowling
review: Harry Potter has never even heard of Hogwarts when the letters start dropping on the doormat at number four, Privet Drive.

author: Paulo Coelho
review: Paulo Coelho's masterpiece tells the mystical story of Santiago, an Andalusian shepherd boy who yearns to travel in search of a worldly treasure.

author: Paula Hawkins
review: Rachel catches the same commuter train every morning. She knows it will wait at the same signal each day, overlooking a row of back gardens.

author: Herman Melville
review: Moby-Dick is an 1851 novel by American writer Herman Melville. The book is the sailor Ishmael's narrative of the obsessive quest of Ahab.

author: Leo Tolstoy
review: War and Peace broadly focuses on Napoleon's invasion of Russia and the impact it had on Tsarist society.

author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
review: Crime and Punishment focuses on the mental anguish and moral dilemmas of Rodion Raskolnikov, an impoverished ex-student in Saint Petersburg.

author: Homer
review: The Odyssey is one of two major ancient Greek epic poems attributed to Homer. It is one of the oldest works of literature read widely today.

author: Charlotte Bronte
review: Jane Eyre follows the experiences of its eponymous heroine, including her growth to adulthood and her love for Mr. Rochester.

author: George Orwell
review: Animal Farm is a allegorical novella by George Orwell, first published in England on 17 August 1945.

author: Ray Bradbury
review: Fahrenheit 451 is a 1953 dystopian novel by American writer Ray Bradbury. It presents a future American society where books are outlawed.

author: J.R.R. Tolkien
review: The Lord of the Rings is an epic high-fantasy novel written by English author and scholar J. R. R. Tolkien.

author: Aldous Huxley
review: Brave New World is a dystopian social science fiction novel by English author Aldous Huxley, written in 1931.

author: Louisa May Alcott
review: Little Women is a novel by American author Louisa May Alcott originally published in two volumes in 1868 and 1869.

author: C.S. Lewis
review: The Chronicles of Narnia is a series of seven fantasy novels by British author C. S. Lewis written between 1949 and 1954.
